COMMITTING: git push is 403 'denied to Onyx-Node' for the fixer too, not only for subagents - the App has no write access to kavopdf/app over HTTPS git. It is not a dead end: the GitHub MCP tool GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (owner kavopdf, repo app, branch main, upserts=[{path,content,encoding:utf-8}]) commits several files atomically and worked for all four commits of this run. The next run should commit that way, then 'git fetch origin main && git reset --hard origin/main' so HEAD matches origin, then chain.py. chain.py's sync check is strict SHA equality and also refuses a dirty tree, and it rewrites CHAIN.json - so commit CHAIN.json again after each chain.py run.

next: Charge the row its REAL height in w:trHeight - not by removing cantSplit, which was measured this run and makes 041122 worse (10 -> 11 pages). The breaking row is one cell 11000 tw (550 pt) wide, nine paragraphs at w:line 240 tw and w:sz 20, 828 characters: the writer charges 9 x 240 + rule = 2220 tw (111 pt) and the render spends ~156 pt, because four paragraphs wrap into two lines in DejaVu where they fit one line in the source face. So in DocxWriter.table(), where rowTwHere and rowLineTw combine into rowHeightTw (around line 6308), charge each paragraph ceil(textWidth / usableCellWidth) line boxes instead of one per source line. A Helvetica advance-width helper is the right metric and it works - PDType1Font.HELVETICA / HELVETICA_BOLD ship with PDFBox, are within a few per cent of DejaVu Sans, and the version of this that was built this run compiled and ran. Then the row is written at ~156 pt, hRule=atLeast is already a floor so the renderer lays it out at 156 pt, 689 + 156 = 845 > 842, and the renderer breaks the row itself at the foot of the sheet - which is what the source does. Do NOT pair it with dropping cantSplit: that combination was measured at 11 pages. Count the documents that change BEFORE measuring (re-convert the corpus and diff the .docx entry by entry; 209 of 213 were byte-identical this run so the diff is cheap and decisive), and pip install scipy before any measurement or every call dies on the tool timeout.

context: TWO ANGLES CLOSED, BOTH MEASURED, AND THE SECOND ONE POINTS THE OTHER WAY. (1) The cantSplit rule cannot close 041122's last extra page: built as specified it fires on 1 of 213 documents and moves nothing; rebuilt on the height the renderer really lays out (max of declared w:trHeight and the w:before+w:line emitted in the row's cells) it fires on 4 of 213 and still moves nothing (041122 10/10 pages identical line for line, Account_Opening_Form_Fillable_filled 10/10 identical, itr-computation 68.12 -> 68.12, 64_newspaper 9.11 -> 9.11; 209 of 213 byte-identical in every zip entry). The breaking row declares 2220 tw (111 pt) and emits 2558 tw (128 pt) of line boxes from a 689.0 pt top edge, so 817 reads as fitting an 842 pt sheet - it renders ~156 pt. (2) The wrap estimate that explains that gap was then BUILT AND MEASURED, and dropping cantSplit on it takes 041122 from 10 pages to ELEVEN: p7 falls from 91 lines to 90 and a one-line page 8 appears. So cantSplit is NOT the lever - with hRule=atLeast a split row leaves a fragment the renderer charges again, and removing the promise costs more than it saves. The engine was reverted to HEAD; the earlier neutral cantSplit change is carried as patches/cantsplit-only-where-keepable.patch (38 lines, applies cleanly) and not in the engine only because DocxWriter.java is 458 KB and the one working commit path takes file contents inline. THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER, measured: the breaking row is ONE cell 11000 tw (550 pt) wide holding NINE paragraphs at w:line 240 tw and w:sz 20, 828 characters; the writer charges 9 x 240 + rule = 2220 tw (111 pt); the render spends ~156 pt (13 lines) because four of those paragraphs wrap into two lines in DejaVu where they fit one line in the source face. OPERATIONAL FACTS THIS RUN PAID FOR: scipy was missing, so every position() call fell back to the 400-step dilation ladder - single-document measurements ran past 200 s and three calls died on the tool timeout before it was found (p2w.py installs scipy inside main(), so a run calling measure_doc() directly never gets it: pip install scipy first). gh api writes are 403 'Resource not accessible by integration', the same wall as git push - GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES is the only write path. round.py --release-fixer REFUSES while pending.py lists work, and pending.py's carry-over item IS HANDOFF.json's own 'next', so a run cannot release cleanly by design: it ends when the platform ends it.
